title: Layton Lights Switch-On: late openings, live music and road closures
imageAlt: Poster for the Layton Christmas Lights Switch-On on Friday 27th November 2026. Event starts from 5.15pm and the lights are switched on at 6.15pm, on Westcliffe Drive, Layton. Special guests, live music, stalls, treasure hunt, book give-away and a brass band. Organised by Layton Together and supported by Forward Project and your local councillors.
summary: The Layton Christmas Lights Switch-On is on Friday 27 November, with Coastal Radio on stage, performers, late-opening shops and community buildings, and road closures from 5pm to 7pm.
intro: The Layton Christmas Lights Switch-On is happening on Friday 27 November, at the start of Westcliffe Drive and Layton Road, with the lights going on around 6:15pm.
paragraphs: The event starts from 5:15pm, with the lights switched on at around 6:15pm to 6:20pm. Coastal Radio will be on stage with performers, and the night also has special guests, live music, stalls, a treasure hunt, a book give-away and a brass band.

Shops and community buildings are opening late so you can make an evening of it, including Hash Browns on Layton Road, Sue at Ninez, Layton Methodist Church, Layton Community House, St Mark's Church and Layton Library. Do pop in, say hello and support them.

Blackpool Council has confirmed temporary road closures around Layton Square from 5pm to 7pm. Drivers are asked to plan their journeys accordingly and to follow the road closure signs. The roads affected are listed below.

The organisers apologise for any inconvenience and thank local residents and businesses for their patience, understanding and support. Is your business staying open late on Friday? Email adam@laytonunlocked.com and we will add it to the list.

title: Layton Community House secures £20,000 National Lottery grant
imageAlt: Graphic reading: £20,000 awarded to Layton Community House from The National Lottery Community Fund.
summary: Layton Community House has been awarded £20,000 from The National Lottery Community Fund, to help it keep providing a welcoming, supportive space for the local community.
intro: Fantastic news for Layton: Layton Community House has been awarded £20,000 in funding from The National Lottery Community Fund.
paragraphs: Layton Community House has announced the award, which will help it continue providing a welcoming and supportive space for the local community, bringing people together, reducing social isolation and offering opportunities to learn new skills and build friendships.

The House, at 5 Grenfell Avenue, is home to a range of regular activities, from sewing and art and craft sessions to free IT help and the Friday infant essentials service. You can see what is on each week on the What's On guide.

In its announcement, Layton Community House thanked National Lottery players for making the funding possible, and its staff, volunteers, trustees and visitors who make the House such a special place. It says it is looking forward to sharing more about the difference the funding will make to the community.

title: Winter Wonderland Weekend
imageAlt: Winter Wonderland Weekend, 27 to 29 November 2026. Posters for the Layton Christmas Lights Switch-On, the Free Christmas Party at The Victory Pub and the StreetLife Festive Family Fun Day at Layton Institute.
summary: Four Christmas events across three days, from the Layton Lights Switch-On on Friday to a free community Christmas party on Sunday, with plenty of free fun along the way.
intro: Blackpool families have a packed Christmas weekend ahead, with four community events across Friday 27, Saturday 28 and Sunday 29 November.
paragraphs: Friday 27 November: the Layton Christmas Lights Switch-On on Westcliffe Drive, organised by Layton Together with Mark Walmsley and his team behind the planning. The event starts from 5:15pm and the lights go on at 6:15pm. There is a treasure hunt for the kids, live music, a brass band, stalls, special guests and a book giveaway, and it is free to attend.

Saturday 28 November, 12pm to 5:30pm: the Bloomfield Brewhouse Christmas Market, with festive stalls and free activities for children with Amy Harvey and Blackpool STEM Club, including a Santa Zipline Challenge.

Saturday 28 November, 6pm to 10pm: the Condor Grove Christmas Lights Switch-On, organised by Lyndsay, with the main switch-on at 7pm. It raises funds for Fylde Kids Foundation, and promises Santa and Mrs Claus arriving by sleigh, live singers, the LIMITLESS girl band, stalls, mascots, hot food, a tombola, raffles and snow machines.

Sunday 29 November, 2pm to 5pm: a free Christmas party and community thank-you at The Victory Pub on Caunce Street, organised by Ameelia Unfiltered with Blackpool Mums & Babies, Mel Bee's and Solo Parents United. Entry, a disco, a buffet, face painting and Santa visits are free, and children get presents and chocolates from Santa. The party also supports a Christmas Present Drive, where donations are welcome but never expected.
Also in Layton that weekend: the Festive Family Fun Day at Layton Institute on Sunday from 1pm to 4pm, and the Music & Memory Social at Layton Library on Saturday morning.
Special thanks to Ameelia Unfiltered for pulling all of this information together.

title: Living Well in Blackpool: free support, all in one place, every Monday
imageAlt: Poster for the Living Well in Blackpool Support Hub. Free support, all in one place. Every Monday, 9.30am to 12.30pm, Layton Methodist, FY3 7DZ. Just turn up. Money feeling tight? Need employment support? Worried about housing? Need food support? Health concerns? Family worries? Want to learn new skills?
summary: Every Monday, 9.30am to 12.30pm at Layton Methodist Church, the Living Well in Blackpool Support Hub brings free help with money, work, housing, food, health, family worries and new skills together in one place.
intro: Money feeling tight? Worried about housing? Need a hand finding work or learning new skills? The Living Well in Blackpool Support Hub is free, with no appointment needed. Just turn up.
paragraphs: The Support Hub runs every Monday from 9.30am to 12.30pm at Layton Methodist Church, Westcliffe Drive, FY3 7DZ, and is supported by Forward Projects. There is a free continental breakfast until 11am, and you do not need to book. Come in, have a chat, and the team will help you find the right support.
A range of local and national services are involved, so one visit can get you talking to the right people. Providers include:

Money: benefit checks, to help make sure people are getting the money they are entitled to, plus Green Doctors, a free Groundwork service giving impartial advice on cutting energy use and managing energy bills at home.
Housing: Shelter, the housing and homelessness charity.
Work and skills: Jobcentre Plus for employment support, and Blackpool & Fylde College for learning new skills.
Health and wellbeing: Active Blackpool, helping people get active, and Empowerment Charity, a Blackpool-based charity supporting people across Blackpool and Lancashire.
Not sure if it is for you? If you are worried about money, work, housing, food, your health, your family or just want to learn something new, it probably is. Pop along on a Monday and see.

title: Festive Express 2026: free Christmas gifts and goodies for local families
imageAlt: Poster for Festive Express 2026, a free festive event from BFriend and Wellbeing. Thursday 3rd December, 2pm to 5:30pm at Forest Gate Baptist Church, Blackpool. Toy station, teen station, Christmas Eve boxes, wrapping station, festive family food ideas, and crafts and activities, all free of charge. Logos: Community First, BFriend and Wellbeing, The National Lottery Community Fund.
summary: BFriend & Wellbeing's annual Festive Express returns on Thursday 3 December at Forest Gate Baptist Church, with free Christmas gifts and goodies for local families. No referral, appointment or paperwork needed.
intro: Last year the Festive Express helped over 100 families with presents, food parcels and Christmas extras. This year, the organisers hope to make an even bigger difference.
paragraphs: The annual Festive Express is run by BFriend & Wellbeing, part of Community First Blackpool, Wyre & Fylde, and takes place at Forest Gate Baptist Church on Thursday 3 December, from 2pm to 5:30pm. It is an afternoon of Christmas gifts, festive goodies and community spirit, with marketplace-style stalls where everything is free.

There are no referrals, appointments or paperwork. Everyone is welcome: just collect your tickets on arrival and exchange them for items. On the day you will find a toy station, a teen station, Christmas Eve boxes, a wrapping station, festive family food ideas, crafts and activities and a free pop-up cafe. The poster also carries The National Lottery Community Fund logo.

Want to help? The organisers are still welcoming donations, volunteers, raffle prizes and support with storage and transport. Donations can be dropped off at Community First, Abingdon Street, Blackpool, until Wednesday 2 December. Please donate toys unwrapped, clean and in good condition. Sharing the event with friends and family helps too.

title: Blackpool Stanley Youth Presentation Celebrations start this week
imageAlt: Poster from Blackpool Stanley Rugby League Club, established 1979. Youth Presentation Celebrations: Saturday 28th November, Under 10s. Friday 4th December, Under 12s and Under 14s. Saturday 12th December, Stanley Scamps. One Club. One Stanley.
summary: Blackpool Stanley Rugby League Club's youth presentation celebrations run from Saturday 28 November to Saturday 12 December, recognising a fantastic year of rugby for the club's young players.
intro: It is presentation time at Blackpool Stanley, with four celebration dates for the club's young players, from the Under 10s to the Stanley Scamps.
paragraphs: Blackpool Stanley Rugby League Club are celebrating another fantastic year of rugby, recognising the hard work, commitment, development and achievements of their young players. The club says it is also a chance to bring everyone together, celebrate friendships and make memories.
The dates announced are: Saturday 28 November for the Under 10s, Friday 4 December for the Under 12s and the Under 14s, and Saturday 12 December for the Stanley Scamps.

Thank you from the club to all its players, parents, families, coaches and volunteers. Their message: every player matters, every effort counts, and every achievement deserves celebrating. Follow Blackpool Stanley Rugby League Club on Facebook for the latest updates, and ask the club for times and venues for each age group.

title: Local businesses wanted: sponsors and raffle prizes for the Christmas fundraiser
imageAlt: Poster from Ameelia Unfiltered. Local business owners, want to get your business noticed whilst making a difference? Looking for event sponsors and raffle prizes, supporting children and struggling families across Blackpool, Fylde and Wyre this Christmas. Logos for Blackpool Mums and Babies by Ameelia, Mel Bee's Amusements and Solo Parents United CIC. Message me to get involved.
summary: The organisers of the free Christmas Party at The Victory Pub on Sunday 29 November are looking for local businesses to sponsor the event or donate raffle, auction and tombola prizes.
intro: Local business owners are being invited to get noticed while making a difference, by backing a Christmas fundraiser that supports children and struggling families across Blackpool, Fylde and Wyre.
paragraphs: Ameelia Unfiltered is organising the Christmas fundraiser and thank-you party at The Victory Pub on Sunday 29 November, from 2pm to 5pm, together with Blackpool Mums & Babies, Mel Bee's Amusements and Solo Parents United CIC. The party is also a thank-you to everyone who has supported the Christmas present drive.
Some prizes and sponsors have already come forward, and the organisers would love a few more businesses to get involved. They are asking for event sponsors and for raffle, auction or tombola prizes.

Prizes do not have to be physical. A voucher, a meal out, a beauty treatment, house cleaning, handyman services, a car clean, or even an hour of your time offering a service could all make a brilliant prize.
In return, the organisers will promote each business across all of their pages, for some local exposure while backing a good cause. You do not have to be a big business to make a big difference.
To get involved, message Ameelia on Facebook. Sharing this story with a business owner who might help is a big help too.
Special thanks to Ameelia Unfiltered for sharing the call-out.

title: Lay a Brick: build a future
imageAlt: Poster for the Lay a Brick campaign for the Layton Youth and Skills Hub. Lay a brick, build a future. Five pounds per brick. Sponsor a brick and receive your own thank-you certificate, with the option to have your name included in the Hall of Fame. Scan the QR code to sponsor a brick today. Other payment methods available on request. Layton Methodist Forward Project, Charity No. 1194986.
summary: A campaign to help build the new Layton Youth & Skills Hub, one £5 brick at a time. Around £270,000 of the £500,000 target is already secured.
intro: Layton Methodist Church and Forward Project have launched the Lay a Brick campaign to help build the new Layton Youth & Skills Hub.
paragraphs: Around £270,000 has already been secured towards a £500,000 target, and the campaign is asking the community to help with the rest.

For £5 per brick, supporters help create a space where local young people can meet, learn new skills and access opportunities. Anyone who gives their contact details receives a thank-you certificate, and can choose to have their name added to the Hall of Fame.
Donations are taken securely online through the campaign's fundraising partner, Give A Little. Other payment methods are available on request.
Every brick makes a difference, and sharing the campaign helps too.
